result.response:
The requirement in `requirement.feature` states that stopping a suspended stopwatch must not include the time elapsed while suspended.

### Root Cause
In [`StopWatch.java`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_55_group_d_fix/src/java/org/apache/commons/lang/time/StopWatch.java#L114-L121), the `stop()` method unconditionally updated `stopTime = System.currentTimeMillis();` regardless of whether the stopwatch was running or suspended. Because `suspend()` already recorded the `stopTime` at suspension, calling `stop()` on a suspended stopwatch inadvertently overwrote `stopTime` with the current time, adding the suspended duration to the total elapsed time.

### Solution
Updated [`stop()`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_55_group_d_fix/src/java/org/apache/commons/lang/time/StopWatch.java#L118-L120) to only record a new `stopTime` if `runningState == STATE_RUNNING`. If suspended, the existing `stopTime` recorded during suspension is retained.

The patch was generated and saved to `enlightened_fix.patch`. All tests, including the Cucumber verification test, passed successfully.
